clue.text: Anaemic and idle husband given the boot

indicators.note: a husband given the boot is thrown out, so his letter is removed from the word

parts.note: idle talk is shallow, lacking depth or purpose

explanation.surface: A pale, lazy husband is shown the door by his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Sallow describes an unhealthy yellowish pallor, the look of someone who is anaemic.

clue.text: Hedonist bemused by satire

indicators.note: bemused means confused, so the letters of the following words are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker is left puzzled by a piece of satire aimed at him.
explanation.definitionFit: A sybarite is a lover of luxury and pleasure, named after the ancient city of Sybaris.

clue.text: Chess player overdue, says Spooner — one of no account?

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words are exchanged by sound

parts.note: the player with the white pieces is called White, here respelt by its sound
something overdue is late, here respelt by its sound

explanation.surface: A chess player turns up late, and is dismissed as a nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of WHITE LATE gives 'light wait', which is spelt as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightweight is a person of little importance or influence, someone who counts for nothing.

clue.text: Daughter leaving Kentish Town a maiden?

indicators.note: the daughter leaving the town means her letter goes out of its name

parts.note: Dover is a port town in the English county of Kent

explanation.surface: A young woman moves out of a town in Kent, leaving her single status in question.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is also a district of London, which disguises the town meant here. A maiden in cricket is an over in which no runs are scored; the question mark flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a maiden is a set of six balls bowled without conceding runs, one particular kind of over.

clue.text: Emmanuel Macron's deep discomfort?

parts.note: a French speaker would use the French phrase for an unease caused by the deep, that is, the sea

explanation.walkthrough: Macron signals French; 'the deep' is a poetic name for the sea, so the discomfort is French for seasickness.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means 'sickness of the sea', the nausea felt aboard a rolling ship.

clue.text: Made progress with American theologian securing vehicle parked by church

indicators.note: securing means holding something fast within, so the first pieces wrap round the others

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree

indicators.note: the vehicle is parked next to the church, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A US divinity scholar gets ahead after leaving his car outside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To have advanced is to have moved forward or gone on, which is making progress.

clue.text: Speech at Christmas maybe getting an award

indicators.note: the speech comes at Christmas, so the month piece sits right before the speech

parts.note: Christmas falls in December, abbreviated Dec; 'maybe' marks the example
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A Christmas address, like the monarch's annual broadcast, earns someone a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoration is a medal or honour conferred on someone, such as a knighthood or military medal.

clue.text: I almost expose my bottom

definitions.note: the setter of this puzzle is called Moo, so 'I' is the setter's pseudonym

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to moon is to bare one's buttocks as a prank

explanation.surface: A cheeky confession that the speaker nearly dropped their trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters refer to themselves as 'I' or 'me'; this puzzle's setter is Moo.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter's pseudonym is the name by which the crossword compiler is known, so it stands for the speaker.

clue.text: Rebellion? Reluctantly at first I reveal all

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: to sing, in slang, is to confess everything to the police

explanation.surface: A reluctant rebel finally confesses everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is an uprising or revolt, a popular rebellion against those in power.

clue.text: Posh school in East End that caught king's eye?

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End drop their initial H sounds, so that letter goes

parts.note: Harrow is an exclusive English public school

explanation.surface: A smart school in a poor part of London draws royal attention.
explanation.walkthrough: King Harold was said to have been killed by one of these in the eye at the Battle of Hastings in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says an arrow shot by a Norman archer struck King Harold in the eye at Hastings.

clue.text: Spy on European in pub, one causing annoyance

parts.note: to bug is to plant a listening device on someone

indicators.note: in places the European's letter inside the word for the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Someone eavesdrops on a European drinker in a bar and becomes a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a persistent source of irritation, something that keeps getting on one's nerves.

clue.text: Sid was so cruel!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the surname of Sid ..., bassist of the Sex Pistols
second meaning: savage or deliberately hurtful

explanation.walkthrough: Sid Vicious was the punk bassist of the Sex Pistols, so the first half is his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means savage or wilfully hurtful, and doubles as the punk musician's stage surname.

clue.text: American writer visiting brothel

indicators.note: the writer is visiting the word, staying inside it, so his name is found within its letters

explanation.surface: A US novelist is seen calling at a house of ill repute.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Roth was a celebrated American novelist, author of Portnoy's Complaint and American Pastoral.

clue.text: Compatriot who's a Dolly Parton fan?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone from one's own nation
second meaning, playful: a man who likes country music, Dolly Parton's genre

explanation.walkthrough: Dolly Parton is a country singer, so her fan is read as a lover of country music.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow citizen of one's nation is a fellow national, and a man keen on country songs fits the whimsical reading.

clue.text: Incoherent, as single men when drunk

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Unattached men after a night out become unable to talk sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that is incoherent makes no sense, which is what lacking sense or significance means.

clue.text: Cockney lacking such hope?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the breathy H sound, which Cockney speech drops
second meaning: an ambition or yearning

explanation.walkthrough: In phonetics, the H sound is called an aspirate; Cockneys famously drop it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the breathing out of an H sound in phonetics and a strong desire to achieve something.

clue.text: Set out twice to discover source of sleeping sickness

indicators.note: out signals the letters set out afresh, and twice says the word is used two times over

parts.note: the word set, written out two times as the indicator asks

explanation.surface: Researchers set out twice on expeditions to find what causes a tropical disease.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse fly of Africa carries the parasite that causes sleeping sickness in people.

clue.text: Of prime importance, as power is to MPs

definitions.meaning: second meaning: P, the abbreviation for power, is the middle letter of MPs

explanation.walkthrough: P for power sits in the middle of the letters MPs, so it is literally at the centre of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something principal or key is at the heart of matters; the letter P is likewise at the heart of MPs.

clue.text: Quick dish for a Parisian? Certainly not

definitions.text: Quick dish for a Parisian? Certainly not

parts.words: Quick dish for a Parisian? Certainly not
parts.note: a French dish made from a creature that is famously slow, so anything but quick

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick dish' suggests fast food; the denial points to the slowest of creatures served in French restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: The French delicacy is a snail, cooked with garlic butter, and snails are proverbially slow.

clue.text: Not much money in bank of late

indicators.note: in places the small coin inside the verb for bank

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
a cent is a coin of very little value

explanation.surface: Lately there has been very little cash left in the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means in the near past, which is what 'of late' expresses.

clue.text: Opposed to a holy woman receiving reward

indicators.note: a holy woman receiving the reward takes it inside her letters

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, here a female one
a gain is a benefit or reward

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a saintly woman being given a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: To be against something is to be in opposition to it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Desirable attribute in a would- be monk?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words
second meaning: a beginner in a religious order, not yet professed

explanation.walkthrough: Read as NO VICE, the answer is a virtue; read as one word, it is a probationer in a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a probationary member of a religious community before taking vows, so a trainee monk.

clue.text: Emerged briefly from police department holding weapon up

indicators.note: the department holds the weapon, which goes inside its abbreviation

parts.note: PD is the American abbreviation for police department

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so it is turned round

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: Something briefly appeared from a police station that was keeping a weapon raised.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep out is to show oneself for a moment, appearing briefly before vanishing.

clue.text: Scrooge having change of heart, becoming a socialite?

indicators.note: the heart is the middle letter, and changing it swaps that letter for another

parts.note: Ebenezer Scrooge of A Christmas Carol is the classic miser

explanation.surface: Dickens's Scrooge has a change of heart and becomes a party-goer, as in A Christmas Carol.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter S becomes X; the question mark flags the definition as loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A good mixer is someone who socialises easily, mingling at parties, which a socialite does.

clue.text: Has auntie arranged a merciful release?

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dark question: has someone set up an elderly aunt's assisted death?
explanation.definitionFit: Euthanasia is the painless ending of a life to relieve suffering, often called a mercy killing.

clue.text: Villa guest nursing a fever

indicators.note: the words are nursing the answer, holding it inside them as a nurse holds a patient

explanation.surface: A guest at a holiday villa is looking after someone with a temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old word for a malarial fever with fits of shivering.

clue.text: Reportedly solicit worshipper at Golden Temple

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or said, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: to solicit is to seek or ask for

explanation.surface: Supposedly people go to a famous shrine to ask for something.
explanation.definitionFit: The Golden Temple at Amritsar in India is the holiest shrine of Sikhism, so its worshippers belong to that faith.

clue.text: Superfluity of words, posh for a tart

indicators.note: posh for a means the letter for posh takes the place of the letter A

parts.note: padding is unnecessary material added to lengthen writing
U stands for upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A wordy, snooty description of a loose woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like the insult but is the pastry dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage pudding is a general word for dessert, and a fruit tart is one example.

clue.text: Mark of senility, forgetting time

indicators.note: forgetting something leaves it out, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: dotage is the feeble-minded state of old age
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A sign of growing old is that one starts forgetting the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a small spot or point, a little mark on a surface.

clue.text: Celebrated artist left without wife

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a well-known British artist

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the wife's letter is removed

parts.note: went means left, departed

explanation.surface: A famous painter walked out, abandoning his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means distinguished and highly regarded, so famous or celebrated.

clue.text: Explode outside school one day

indicators.note: outside means the day's word goes round the school's name

parts.note: a date is a particular day
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A bomb goes off one day beyond the school gates.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate is to set off or blow up, as a bomb does.

clue.text: A question about one's king shows spirit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the question word goes round the others

parts.note: why is a question
one's can be read as 'one is', and 'I is' squashed together gives the letters here
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Asking about a monarch reveals courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is a distilled alcoholic drink, and such drinks are called spirits.
